name: Nalli Nihari
subtitle: marrow bones and shank stewed overnight, eaten at dawn

ingredients.note: the marrow is the point; ask for nalli specifically

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp paste, plus julienne to finish

ingredients.note: the thickener; nihari gravy is flour-bound, not reduced

prepNotes: Nihar means dawn. It was cooked overnight on dying coals and eaten at first light, and the long cook is not negotiable.
Nalli is the marrow bone. Serve it with a thin skewer so people can get the marrow out.

steps.text: Brown the onions in the oil until deep and dark. Lift half out and reserve for the top.
Add the ginger and garlic pastes, then the fennel, dry ginger, chilli, turmeric and black cardamom. Fry 3 minutes.
Add the meat and bones and fry hard until sealed and coloured, 10 minutes.
Add 2 litres water, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 3 hours.
steps.tip: The lowest heat you can hold. A hard boil makes the meat stringy rather than soft.

steps.text: Slake the flour in cold water and stir it in. Simmer uncovered 30 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.
steps.tip: Slaked in cold water, always, or it lumps.

steps.text: Finish with garam masala. Serve topped with the reserved onions, ginger julienne and lemon.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and is famously better the next day. Reheat to a full simmer, loosening with hot water.
